thread.title: Market Volatility Bulletin: Stocks Attempt A Recovery, But Settle Flat

author: The Balance of Trade
title: Market Volatility Bulletin: Stocks Attempt A Recovery, But Settle Flat
text:
Market Intro
Global stocks ( VGK , ACWI , SPY ) took the opportunity to recoup after a couple rough weeks as Americans head to the Thanksgiving table. Weakness in Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ) may have played a role in US stocks giving up most of the day’s gains, but at least in the after-hours market the futures are inching back higher.
The EU called out Italy for not keeping its deficit at acceptable levels, opening up a new procedure and potential room for more squabbling amongst various technocrats in the coming weeks and months. Still, European stocks as a group performed well amidst the headline.
CNBC
Retail stocks ( XRT , XLY ) have a lot to prove over the coming several weeks and may generate the verdict as to whether the economy is cooling or if instead, the consumer comes out credit cards a’blazin. Should the retail figures come in strong, volatility could well descend.
Thoughts on Volatility
The other side of tremendous volatility. Click here for a humorous summary of the path of bitcoin over the last year. The fall at this point, in percentage terms, has been exceeded by the cryptocurrency on a couple occasions in its storied history. The story of the rise of bitcoin was quite different from that of the stock market over the last several years.
Equities may very well decide to climb the wall of worry. Today’s surrender of earlier gains shows that we’re not likely to see that just yet, or at least not until the FANGs stabilize. If the group can just calm down some, or better yet decouple in a meaningful way, stocks have a chance as we head into year-end.
By many a measure , US stocks are overpriced. Valuations are more of a long-term generator of returns rather than short term, unless investors suddenly decide en masse that valuations do matter and that they’re too high.
Term Structure
In spite of the fact that SPX dropped as the Wednesday session wore on, the VIX term structure headed south. More surprising still was the fact that VIX9D saw fit to hand back almost four vol points amidst the action. Vol shorts ( SVXY ) really do have a shot here, but they’ll need to hold onto some wins.
Good question, Forward. Daily rebalance is not the same as backwardation or contango. VXX , for instance, is subject to the impact of roll decay, but because the leverage is 1x long, there is no rebalancing.
I have the term structure for October 26 through November 8, skipping some days so as not to clutter the picture. The weighted drop in the M1-M2 term structure over the dates in question was around 17%, while UVXY fell almost double that amount.
There are several factors at play for UVXY’s losses: 1.5x leverage, rebalance decay, as well as at least some benefit from selling contracts on the way down (leveraged funds benefit from momentum). Finally, backwardation likely played a modest, beneficial role.
These instruments are complicated! Simply knowing that suggests how heavily invested in them one should be.
Conclusion If this is your first time reading Market Volatility Bulletin, thanks for giving it a try. If you're a regular, we thank you for your ongoing contributions in the comments section.
Silent Trader added his voice in the most recent MVB to a discussion on how independently the ECB and the Fed run their respective books.
Put in mathematical language, members of the Fed likely analyze their decision set through the lens of partial differential equations, where a tremendous amount of n th order effects come into play. Moreover, the speed at which changes take place can be as important as the changes themselves.
Thank you for reading. Happy Thanksgiving!
